author: ethdreamer
content:
Checked Lighthouse and the new published XMSS cache. The cache contains the two trees needed at genesis. We then build **two future trees per key in the background**—256 new trees for 128 keys. That worker processes keys one at a time, so a few minutes there is plausible.

Keys are marked ready before that background work; signing doesn't wait for it to finish, though it still uses CPU. We persist the extra trees for restart. The `0 ms` log measures cache import after download, rounded to milliseconds.

Could you paste the surrounding `Finished preparing PQ XMSS validator keys` / `Generating PQ XMSS signing trees` logs, and say whether duties actually waited? That will confirm whether your four minutes were background lookahead or a startup delay. The generation log should be clearer about which it is.

author: barnabasbusa
content:
<@&1573329688464720065>  drops its own execution payload whenever its block has blobs 🫠

On pq-devnet-0 under spamoor load, every Silver proposal with blobs is missing its payload. Slots 27314–27336 (0 blobs) were revealed fine; slots 27350–27407 (3–7 blobs each) never were. The Lighthouse VC gets `Unable to publish PQ envelope: 400 … "rejected as invalid"` from Silver's own `POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes`, and peers keep asking for the envelope by root.

Cause: `build_payload_columns` (`crates/columns/src/tile/proposal.rs:273`) only accepts the Gloas `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelopeView` (BLS) layout, so it rejects the XMSS-signed PQ envelope. Blobless envelopes skip that path, which is why only blob blocks break. Same line is on `pq-devnet-0`, `pq-devnet-1` and `main`.

Fix + regression test (fails before, passes after):
- pq-devnet-1: <https://github.com/gattaca-com/pq-silver/pull/48>
- pq-devnet-0: <https://github.com/gattaca-com/pq-silver/pull/50>
